canonicalCompany.name: Chicago Parking Meters, LLC
canonicalCompany.description: Chicago-based concessionaire that operates, manages and maintains approximately 36,000 on-street metered parking spaces under the City of Chicago's 75-year concession and markets the system through ParkChicago.

mergeDecision.rationale: No repository-company merge is required because only one repository company ID exists. The potential new task is the same legal entity and should resolve to the existing canonical record rather than create a second company.

ownershipDecisions.rationale: ADIA remains an indirect owner through Deeside Investments, Inc. The sellers accepted Stonepeak affiliates' bid for a proposed 100% transfer, but City approval and consummation remained outstanding as of the as-of date, so ADIA must stay active with a pending-exit flag.

Allianz SE remains an indirect owner through Deeside Investments, Inc.; Allianz Capital Partners is the attributable infrastructure manager within Allianz Global Investors. The accepted Stonepeak bid is still subject to City approval and closing, so the Allianz exposure remains active but pending exit.

North Haven Infrastructure Partners, attributable to Morgan Stanley Infrastructure Partners, remains the 50.1% owner within the current Morgan Stanley-Allianz-ADIA consortium. The accepted Stonepeak bid remained subject to City approval and consummation as of the as-of date, so the Morgan Stanley exposure stays active with a pending-exit flag and no exit year.

listReadyMilestones.event: The 75-year Chicago metered-parking concession reached financial close; the ownership consortium included Morgan Stanley, Allianz Capital Partners and ADIA.
Chicago Parking Meters requested City approval for the proposed transfer of all ownership interests to Stonepeak affiliates after the sellers accepted Stonepeak's bid.

evidence.title: About
evidence.evidenceSummary: Establishes the legal and operating identity, CPM and ParkChicago aliases, concessionaire role, approximately 36,000 on-street metered spaces, 2009 operating start and the 75-year concession.

evidence.title: Ordinance authorizing approval of the proposed ownership transfer of Chicago Parking Meters, LLC
evidence.evidenceSummary: Names Deeside Investments, Inc. as a direct owner and Allianz SE and ADIA as its indirect owners; states that the sellers accepted Stonepeak affiliates' bid, that the buyer would own 100% after consummation, and that City approval was requested on March 12, 2026.

evidence.title: Innovative Infrastructure Delivery: Chicago Parking Meter Analysis
evidence.evidenceSummary: Confirms the 75-year concession, February 2009 close and original consortium including Morgan Stanley, Allianz Capital Partners and ADIA.

evidence.title: Infrastructure equity
evidence.evidenceSummary: Lists Chicago Parking Meters as an Allianz Global Investors infrastructure-equity investment example in Chicago, United States.

evidence.title: Our history
evidence.evidenceSummary: Confirms that Allianz Capital Partners joined Allianz Global Investors in 2018, supporting attribution of the Allianz ownership exposure to the requested manager.

evidence.title: Concessionaire preps Chicago Parking Meters sale
evidence.evidenceSummary: Reports February 2009 financial close and sponsor stakes of 50.1% for North Haven Infrastructure Partners, 25.0% for Allianz Capital Partners and 24.9% for ADIA; it also identifies ParkChicago as an alias.

evidence.title: Ald. Ervin proposes 'infrastructure trust' to weigh taking back parking meters
evidence.evidenceSummary: Identifies the Morgan Stanley-Allianz-ADIA consortium as the current owner and reports that the City Council had until September 30 to accept or reject Stonepeak's offer, confirming that the transfer remained unclosed.

proposedChanges.rationale: The current owners accepted Stonepeak's bid, but the transfer remained subject to City approval and consummation; ADIA therefore remains active pending exit.
Allianz is part of the same selling ownership structure, so its relation should receive the same legally pending-exit treatment rather than remain unqualified active.
North Haven Infrastructure Partners holds the 50.1% Morgan Stanley-attributable interest and remains part of the current selling consortium; the relation therefore stays active pending legal closing.

proposedChanges.after: Mar 12, 2026 - CPM requested City approval for a proposed transfer that would give Stonepeak affiliates 100% ownership after consummation.
proposedChanges.rationale: This is the attributable pending-exit milestone and must not be recorded as a completed divestiture.
The candidate resolves to the same legal entity, geography, website and concession; no second repository company should be created.
